question: Using Section 8B.03 and Figure 8B-2, describe the vertical order of a passive-crossing assembly with multiple tracks and a YIELD or STOP sign, and state when the Number of Tracks plaque is required.
model_answer: Direct Answer: At a passive grade crossing with multiple tracks, the assembly is arranged top to bottom as: the Crossbuck (R15-1) sign at the top, the inverted-T Number of Tracks (R15-2P) plaque mounted directly below the Crossbuck, and the YIELD (R1-2) or STOP (R1-1) sign below that on the same support (unless placed on a separate support per the exception noted). The Number of Tracks plaque is required whenever there are two or more tracks at the grade crossing. Standards (mandatory): - "The Grade Crossing (R15-1) sign (see Figure 8B-1), commonly identified as the Crossbuck sign, shall be retroreflective white with the words RAILROAD CROSSING in black lettering, mounted as shown in Figure 8B-2." - "If there are two or more tracks at a grade crossing, the number of tracks shall be indicated on a supplemental Number of Tracks (R15-2P) plaque (see Figure 8B-1) of inverted T shape mounted below the Crossbuck sign in the manner shown in Figure 8B-2." - "A Crossbuck Assembly shall consist of a Crossbuck (R15-1) sign, and a Number of Tracks (R15-2P) plaque if two or more tracks are present, that complies with the provisions of Section 8B.03, and either a YIELD (R1-2) or STOP (R1-1) sign installed on the same support, except as provided in Paragraph 10 of this Section. YIELD or STOP signs used at passive grade crossings shall be installed in compliance with the provisions of Section 2B.18, and Figures 8B-2 and 8B-3." - "As a minimum, one Crossbuck sign shall be used on each highway approach to every highway-rail grade crossing, alone or in combination with other traffic control devices." - "On each approach to a highway-rail grade crossing and, if used, on each approach to a highway-LRT grade crossing, the Crossbuck sign shall be installed on the right-hand side of the highway on each approach to the grade crossing." Visual evidence: - [Image 5] Page 1036 (Figure 8B-2, "Crossbuck Assembly with a YIELD or STOP Sign on the Crossbuck Sign Support") shows the vertical order — Crossbuck at top (approximately 9 ft mounting height to sign center), the "3 TRACKS" inverted-T plaque immediately below, and the YIELD or STOP sign below the plaque — along with notes that YIELD/STOP signs are used only at passive crossings and a STOP sign only if an engineering study determines it is appropriate. - [Image 1] Figure 8E-5 (p.1039) illustrates the same top-to-bottom arrangement (Crossbuck, "2 TRACKS" plaque, then YIELD or STOP sign) on a single support at a pathway or sidewalk grade crossing. - [Image 4] Page 1038 shows the same Figure 8E-5 layout within Section 8E.05, confirming the assembly order at pathway/sidewalk crossings. - [Image 3] Page 1080 contains Section 8B.04 provisions confirming the assembly requirements, including that a YIELD sign is the default device unless an engineering study supports a STOP sign. - [Image 2] Page 1041 provides related Section 8B.04 mounting-height standards for YIELD or STOP signs on the Crossbuck support. Citations: - Section 8B.03 Standard §1 (p.993) - Section 8B.03 Standard §6 (p.993) - Section 8B.04 Standard §1 (p.995) - Section 8B.03 Standard §3 (p.993) - Section 8B.03 Standard §7 (p.993) - Figure 8E-5 (p.1039) - Page 1036 - Page 1038 - Page 1041 - Page 1080
gold_answer: The Crossbuck is at the top, the inverted-T Number of Tracks plaque is directly below it, and the YIELD or STOP sign is below the plaque on the support. The Number of Tracks plaque is required when two or more tracks are present.
